Program Description

MIS is designed to produce students who combine knowledge of business processes with practical (hands-on) knowledge of building information systems. MIS Graduates can start or join a computer consulting company specializing in providing turnkey business systems to small businesses or organizational units in larger companies.

Program Description

The Management Department at Wichita State University provides programs and courses beneficial to students to become effective leaders and business professionals within the workforce. Programs available include Business Administration, Entrepreneurship (with an optional emphasis in Real Estate), Human Resource Management, International Business and Management.
149:
Wichita State University’s Bachelor of Science (BS) in computer engineering will prepare students for a high-paying career in a large number of industries and governmental organizations. Students will have access to some of the best labs and technology in the country—and the chance to work and research with faculty and industry professionals on campus and in Kansas’ center of industry.

Computer engineering students have the opportunity to apply their knowledge to real industry problems in the Robotics and Automation Lab, part of Wichita State University’s National Institute for Aviation Research (NIAR).

Wichita State University’s vast industry connections, and work-based learning for every major, gives computer engineering students the chance to grow their professional network, gain practical experience, earn a paycheck—and open doors to their dream careers.
66c:
Program Description

The Bachelor of Science in Health Science program at Wichita State University provides a foundation in liberal arts and sciences, along with a core health sciences curriculum. Students will develop a broad understanding of social and scientific principles, obtain a clinical foundation, and explore political, legal, social, multicultural, and ethical issues in healthcare.

Students in this program will expand interdisciplinary understanding and collaboration among the health professions. Students also learn how to apply scientific knowledge, humanistic values, critical analysis, and a systematic approach to solving problems.

Students focus in the basic sciences during the first two years of the program, followed by more focused study in the health sciences during the last two years.
661p:
A Master of Arts (MA) in Economics and Quantitative Analysis from Wichita State’s AACSB-accredited Barton School of Business offers students three specialized options to choose from—data analytics, financial economics or international economics. All three options will equip students with a broad understanding of the overall economic environment, which will help them as they advance their careers or pursue further study in Economics. A no-concentration option is also available for students who want to to customize their program of study.

This graduate program has been classified as STEM (CIP Code 45.0603). Students in our program can apply for a 24-month STEM extension of F1 Optional Practical Training (OPT).

Program Description

The mission of the exercise science program is to promote health and well-being through research, teaching, and service/outreach in the study of physical activity. Essential aspects of these efforts are the preparation of scholars and professionals in the study of exercise science at the undergraduate level and graduate levels. In addition, we educate the public and theUniversity community in the scientific aspects of physical activity, especially exercise, sport, and the movements of daily life.

Exercise science is a multifaceted field of studyin which movement or physical activity is the intellectual focus. This includes exercise of improvement of health and physical fitness and activities of daily living, work, sport, and play. It involves special population groups such as children and older adults; persons with disability, injury, or disease; and athletes.
15m:
Program Description

The Barton School of Business offers the Master of Business Administration (MBA) through faculty in the accounting; economics; finance, real estate and decision sciences; management and marketing departments, as well as in other colleges of the university. The MBA program is designed to prepare men and women for responsible positions of professional leadership in business, government, health-related organizations and other institutions. The program concentrates on general management, with particular attention given to developing within the student an understanding of the organization as an integrated system. Areas of concentration are available for those students wishing to focus their elective coursework in a specialized area. Concentration areas currently available are finance, entrepreneurship and innovation, health care administration, and business analytics and information management. The total hours required of students and the level at which they begin participation in the MBA program depend on their academic preparation. The total number of hours required for completion of an MBA ranges from 36 to 48. Classes are taken for graduate credit and all of the courses are offered in the evening.
